strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear articulation of challenges in multi-view 3D scene graph generation and safety-critical implications for robotics
Novel re-shot guided uncertainty estimation approach that creatively leverages reconstructed point cloud geometry to assess caption reliability from optimal viewpoints

Strong empirical results on target dataset with meaningful improvements (node precision 0.82 vs 0.68, edge precision 0.91 vs 0.82) and significant computational speedup (2/3 reduction in mapping time)
Comprehensive pipeline with three complementary components (dynamic downsampling, re-shot uncertainty, object-level RAG) that are well-motivated and carefully designed
Thorough ablation study (Figure 3) convincingly demonstrates that each component contributes meaningfully to overall performance
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and good reproducibility efforts (detailed implementation details, promise to release code, public dataset)
Addresses a genuine limitation of prior crop-only approaches by incorporating full 3D object geometry
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental scope: evaluation restricted to single synthetic Replica dataset; no evaluation on real-world RGB-D data, ScanNet, or other benchmarks that have become standard in recent 3DSG literature

Missing comparisons to recently published methods (Werby et al. 2024, Koch et al. 2024, Maggio et al. 2024); only comparisons are against ConceptGraphs variants from 2024, limiting assessment of relative progress

Insufficient rigor in human evaluation: no inter-annotator agreement metrics (Cohen's κ, Fleiss' κ), unclear annotator background/expertise, no confidence intervals, no significance testing, small sample sizes (~45-67 objects per scene)

Uncertainty estimation methodology is ad-hoc: clustering strategy for selecting 'top-1 cluster' lacks principled justification; no validation that predicted uncertainty correlates with actual caption errors; 50% low-uncertainty threshold appears arbitrary

Re-shot image generation has unjustified design choices: fixed view quality score weights (α=β=0.2) without sensitivity analysis; uniform hemisphere sampling without principled justification; bounding box diagonal as scale proxy fails for elongated objects

Incomplete computational cost analysis: overall end-to-end pipeline time not reported; rendering costs for re-shot images not quantified; RAG retrieval and VLM inference costs not analyzed; practical deployment viability unclear
Dynamic downsampling contribution is confounded in ablation studies and cannot be isolated independently; no comparison with alternative adaptive downsampling strategies
RAG strategy is overly simplistic: position-based nearest-neighbor retrieval is crude; top-50% uncertainty threshold and single-neighbor retrieval are arbitrary choices without ablation
Foundation model dependency not addressed: results tied to specific model versions (GPT-4-0613, GPT-4o-mini); no discussion of robustness to model updates; prompt strategies may be brittle
Limited novelty in edge caption generation: mostly derivative from ConceptGraphs with expanded relation types; predefined 8-category relations still constrain vocabulary

Semantic segmentation evaluation (Section 4.3) relies on synthetic ground-truth from SemanticNeRF; ablation uses GPT-4o as semantic assigner, confounding uncertainty estimation with LLM capability; limited applicability to real-world scenarios
No failure case analysis: case study shows only success case; no per-category performance breakdown; no investigation of when re-shot uncertainty estimation fails or underperforms

Unclear quality of comparison baselines: ConceptGraphs-Detector performs much worse than ConceptGraphs on nodes (0.58 vs 0.68); explanation missing, making it unclear whether improvements stem from weakness of baselines or strength of proposed method
Statistical validation concerns: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; human evaluation lacks rigor typical for open-vocabulary tasks

strengths: Well-motivated problem with compelling real-world relevance: clearly articulates semantic inconsistencies in cross-view aggregation with effective visual examples
Novel re-shot guided uncertainty estimation: creative approach to synthesize optimal viewpoints from reconstructed geometry, elegantly breaking passive observation dependency

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: real-world benchmarks (SceneFun3D, FunGraph3D), fine-grained human evaluation with inter-annotator agreement (κ=0.76), systematic ablations, robustness testing with noise injection, and successful robot deployment
Strong empirical results: 90.2% R@10 on SceneFun3D vs 87.8% baseline; 0.82 vs 0.68 human-evaluated precision; consistent improvements across multiple metrics
Thoughtful engineering: dynamic downsampling strategy (Eq. 1), interpretable multi-factor view scoring (Eq. 2), computational efficiency through selective rendering, composite image prompting
Clear presentation with effective visualizations that convey intuition and methodology
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: view selection scoring uses standard metrics (visibility, orientation, prior alignment) without principled justification; RAG module is simplistic nearest-neighbor retrieval; framework largely assembles existing components (SAM, CLIP, VLMs) without deep innovation

Uncertainty metric lacks rigor: cosine similarity between caption embeddings as reliability proxy is unjustified; no theoretical foundation for why consistency implies correctness; caption clustering process never detailed (algorithm, threshold, consensus formation); 50% uncertainty threshold appears arbitrary

Evaluation scope limitations: only 20-24 scenes per benchmark with limited diversity (all indoor, semantic-rich); human evaluation on only 8 Replica scenes; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; modest improvements with Ours-LLaVA (73.6% vs 70.7%) suggest model capacity confounding

Incomplete methodology justification: why concatenate re-shot and crop images? why position-based retrieval over semantic relevance? why 8 relationship categories? prompt design ad-hoc; parameter sensitivity analysis deferred to supplement; no analysis of performance scaling with object complexity or geometric degradation

Missing failure case analysis: no discussion of when re-shot synthesis fails (transparent/reflective objects, thin structures, dynamic scenes); limited robustness evaluation beyond pose noise; no analysis of dependence on SAM segmentation and CLIP embedding quality

Generalization concerns: all datasets are indoor semantic scenes; no outdoor, cluttered, or dynamic evaluation; injected noise (1°, 0.02m) labeled 'extreme' but represents modest perturbations; method fundamentally dependent on good 3D reconstruction quality

Incomplete runtime analysis and scalability claims: '2.49s per Replica scene' lacks breakdown; 'minimal computational overhead' for rendering 64 views unsubstantiated; offline system only despite claims of future online integration; cost analysis (~$0.50/scene) superficial

Comparison fairness issues: baseline comparisons marked with '*' indicate different 3D node setups; extension to 8 relationship categories vs baseline complicates attribution of gains; limited controlled ablations isolating method contribution from model capacity

Simplistic RAG design: nearest-neighbor retrieval lacks sophistication; only using top-1 neighbor restrictive; no exploration of retrieval diversity or ranking alternatives; spatial proximity may not correlate with semantic relevance

Presentation overclaiming: 'superior' improvements sometimes <2% margins; 'active photographer' metaphor loose (simulating views from geometry rather than active capture); limited societal impact discussion for safety-critical robotics applications

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear articulation of semantic inconsistency issues in existing 3DSG methods; the 'passive observer to active photographer' conceptual framing is intuitive and compelling

Novel application of active re-shot verification combined with object-level RAG for uncertainty-guided refinement; view quality scoring system (Eq. 2) is thoughtfully designed with three complementary heuristics

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple benchmarks (SceneFun3D, FunGraph3D, Replica) with quantitative metrics, human evaluation (κ=0.76 inter-annotator agreement), stress testing with pose noise, and real robotic deployment

Strong empirical results with consistent improvements over state-of-the-art (90.2% R@10 vs 87.8%, 0.82 vs 0.68 node precision); robustness demonstrated with only ~3% degradation under severe geometric noise

Practical system design with efficient runtime optimizations: dynamic downsampling balances detail preservation with memory efficiency; only top-scoring view triggers rendering/VLM querying (~0.26s per object)
Extensive supplementary materials with detailed hyperparameter ablations, case studies, algorithm pseudocode, and complete prompt templates supporting reproducibility
Clear presentation with well-organized methodology, informative figures, and thorough ablation studies isolating component contributions
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: re-shot rendering, object-level retrieval, and downsampling are straightforward applications of existing techniques; primary contribution is effective system integration rather than novel algorithms

Fundamental mismatch between claimed robotics focus and offline-only processing: method requires complete data collection before scene graph generation, contradicting real-time requirements; 'future online applications' claim feels disconnected from current system design

Oversimplified uncertainty quantification: using 1 - (average similarity of top K-means cluster with fixed K=3) lacks principled justification; arbitrary cluster count, vulnerable to uniformly low similarities, no comparison with entropy-based or epistemic uncertainty measures

Incomplete characterization of reconstruction quality dependency: while pose noise tested, real-world sensor artifacts (depth discontinuities, reflections, occlusions) only briefly discussed; no systematic evaluation on highly cluttered/partially observed scenes where geometry degrades

Insufficient analysis of failure modes: only success cases shown; no systematic characterization of object categories, scene types, or imaging conditions where performance degrades or re-shot rendering fails
Limited scale of human evaluation: only 8 Replica scenes with κ=0.76 (substantial but not perfect agreement); no per-scene or per-object category breakdowns; ambiguous disagreement sources

Edge generation contribution overstated: paper acknowledges improvements come primarily from node accuracy; constraining open-vocabulary framework to 8 predefined relation categories somewhat contradicts positioning; edge reasoning uses standard few-shot prompting

Fair comparison issues: Ours-GPT uses GPT-4o while baselines use different models; makes it difficult to isolate algorithmic contributions from model capacity; API cost (~$0.50/scene) not discussed for scalability
Missing runtime analysis: no end-to-end latency comparison vs baselines; individual component costs reported but total pipeline overhead unclear; scalability to 100+ object scenes not addressed

Hyperparameter sensitivity underexplored: many introduced parameters (δ_sample, δ_sim, α_prior, α_horiz, α_vis, K); transfer across datasets/platforms/environments not discussed; parameter selection rationale incomplete
